pattern: Myth vs fact supplement carousel, remade from the Turkish 'Hangi takviyeleri alırsam?' and 'Takviyeden önce...' doctor and dietitian listicles
why: The persona already searches 'which supplement should I take' on Instagram, so busting four common assumptions one per slide answers that question with their own data instead of another generic list.

body: Gerçek: Doktor ve diyetisyenler sürecin içinde.

slides.issues: Clean, readable headline over a solid dark gradient. The open pill bottle with capsules is a familiar stock-style flat lay, so it blends into the feed. The hook question is generic. A sharper tension line would stop the scroll better, such as a number or a 'you are probably wasting money' angle. The subline is small but readable.

The real product is visible: the Dynova site on a phone with the Health and Nutrition cards. This is a strong proof slide. The phone mockup is slightly flat and floats on a blurred background, which makes it feel like a template. Some screen copy is small but acceptable. The headline sits on a busy light background but still holds.

An obvious Unsplash-style stock photo of a woman on a couch with a laptop. It is generic and unrelated to gene report content. The body text runs over a busy area with the book and mug, and the second body line is tight. The visual does not support the claim that the reports cover nutrition, skin, and aging.

final.notes: The gate passes: the Dynova site on a phone appears on slide 2 and the dynova.health CTA is on slide 6. The myth/fact structure is coherent and the copy is compliant, including 'Rapor teşhis koymaz.' The main weaknesses are stock and AI imagery on slides 3, 4, and 6, a generic hook on slide 1, and text overlapping faces and hands on slides 4 and 6. Consider showing the real test kit or report screens on slides 3 and 5 to strengthen product presence and trust.

slides.issues: Headline reads well on the dark gradient, but the purple 'takviye' has weaker contrast than the white words. The spilled pill bottle on beige is a very common stock image, so it blends into every supplement ad in the feed. The question hook is relevant but generic. Nothing signals genetics or personalization yet, which is the actual twist. The 1/6 counter is fine.

rounds.notes: The gate passes: the real Dynova site appears on slide 2 and the dynova.health CTA is on slide 6. The myth/fact structure is clear and the copy is tight, but the imagery is mostly recognizable stock (pills, couch laptop, white-coat doctor, beauty portrait), which drags native feel into the 60s and 70s. Biggest wins: 1) Put the genetic angle into the slide 1 hook, for example 'Takviye seçerken genlerine baktın mı?'. 2) Show real product screens on slides 3 to 5, such as a report sample, the expert consultation flow and the KVKK page. 3) Add a darker scrim on slide 2. 4) Move the logo off the face on slide 6 and end on the kit or app. Purple accent words consistently lose contrast on mid-tone areas, so consider a lighter lavender or adding a subtle shadow.
